study.question: Does replacing the appended attention summary with its deviation from within-group uniform pooling improve on the original summary, and does that benefit specifically depend on target queries, at identical allocated capacity and frozen full-data training?
study.hypothesis: Source inspection shows that the equal-group uniform readout is the mean of occupied original group pools. The appended positive attention summary contains that baseline as well as within-group deviations. This source-level overlap is a consequential uncertainty, not a measured optimization failure. Explicitly exposing signed within-group deviations may give the classifier easier access to selective evidence while retaining all original pools, count statistics and joint histograms. The incumbent AUC is 0.6202303848951921 versus paired_match 0.6191087654101018 and target_separate 0.6153351063827704. Target/context gains have been mixed: initial hybrid context exceeded target; balanced target exceeded context by 0.000222325. Magnitude retention (0.619633), group normalization (0.619911), density allocation (0.619970), slots (0.619865), explicit product interaction (0.619414), and uniform-floor smoothing (0.620069) did not improve the incumbent. These unsuccessful implementations do not establish that attention centering will help or that target conditioning is causal. Floor0 controls reproduced existing seed42 outcomes exactly; that is operational reproducibility, not independent seed support.

nearest_work.difference: Inherits target-related weighted pooling and relation scoring through local ancestors. DIN explicitly abandons softmax to retain interest intensity; these models instead retain the local frozen grouped softmax and pooled-norm matching. New contrast subtracts the equal-group uniform contribution before normalization. This is not an exact DIN reproduction.

nearest_work.source_ref: queryformer-paper-v1; arxiv:2609.16548v1; primary section5.2 Table4 lines224-248
nearest_work.difference: Its query-generation replacement motivates checking query source, but does not establish a local query bottleneck or complementarity. No query generator, bridge, multiview stack or source split is imported. This proposal changes value aggregation relative to a known group baseline while fixing the local scorer.

Preserve complete paired_match features, scorer, field reads, head width, and parameter initialization. Replace only appended raw value by a centered raw value, crossed with query source. All four cells use identical zero-fallback normalization; raw controls check equivalence to the incumbent.

Floor smoothing moves positive attention weights toward within-group uniform weights and did not improve validation. Centering instead subtracts that uniform baseline, producing signed coefficients whose group mass is zero; it is not smoothing or an attention entropy penalty. General centering/difference pooling priority is unverified: indexed searches for centering and differential returned no matches, which is missing evidence rather than novelty evidence.

inherited_components: All causal inputs, first-six-day training, natural label ratio, fixed history_limit128 and host scoring/splits. Static snapshot as-of dates remain undocumented.
Original category/brand/action/log-age embeddings, four match-group means, four count statistics and64 action-age count histogram cells.
DIN-style relation scorer, separate category/brand reads, equal occupied-group allocation and pooled-norm matching concept.
Identical F*d+5*d+68 classifier width (436 at F18,d16), hidden128/64, Adam default and learning rate0.001. No extra learned parameters, supervision, inputs or memory.
study.proposed_difference: For occupied group g, define u_i=1/(K*n_g) and inherited per-field weights w_ci,w_bi. Compute r=sum[w_ci*c_i+w_bi*b_i+0.5*(w_ci+w_bi)*h_i], b=sum[u_i*(c_i+b_i+h_i)] and delta=sum[(w_ci-u_i)*c_i+(w_bi-u_i)*b_i+0.5*(w_ci+w_bi-2*u_i)*h_i]=r-b. Each signed field coefficient sums to zero in each group. Centered cells append delta; raw cells append r. Normalize the chosen vector to ||global pooled history|| when norm>1e-6, otherwise return zero, in all cells. The common zero fallback differs from ancestor pooled fallback only for degenerate raw vectors; diagnostics compare both raw-normalized formulas and require a reported caveat or follow-up if materially different. Baseline subtraction is differentiable through shared values; nothing is detached. Both raw and centered paths are computed in all cells. Centering changes the exposed direction and gradient geometry, not available causal information or classifier capacity; it is not orthogonal residualization or proven noise removal.
predictions: Primary exploratory utility: center_target full-validation AUC exceeds raw_target, incumbent0.6202303848951921 and both frozen source bests; logloss and measured training/inference costs are reported independently.

For target-specific centering support, (AUC_center_target-AUC_raw_target) exceeds (AUC_center_context-AUC_raw_context), with centered target also exceeding centered context. A main centering effect shared by queries supports only a query-independent representation explanation.

Candidate-supplied first512 diagnostics should show zero signed group mass, neutral baseline equal to mean occupied original pools, delta=r-b, zero masked mass, finite empty/zero-length logits and padding/permutation invariance. All-singleton occupied groups should give zero centered raw values; the independent scalar oracle also checks uniform weights and fixed-score group-offset invariance. These are execution/algebra checks, not utility or causal proof.

New nondegenerate summaries match the same pooled norm; fixed-score target/context and centered/raw replacements may affect logits, demonstrating execution only. All cells should have17147171 parameters (68483 dense,17078688 embeddings) on frozen metadata.
falsifiers: No centered target improvement versus raw_target and incumbent leaves incremental utility unsupported. A single failed implementation does not refute all centering mechanisms.
Equal or larger centering benefit with context queries, or centered context matching/beating centered target, leaves target-specific complementarity unsupported.

Broken group-sum/subtraction/neutral-pool identities, nonfinite outputs, padding dependence, materially nonzero all-singleton/uniform residuals, or unexpected capacity differences invalidate the intended contrast until fixed; failed costs remain charged.

A gain explained by repeated-seed variation, materially changed zero fallback, small-residual normalization amplification, or extra measured cost is not sufficient evidence of the proposed optimization explanation.
alternative_explanations: Signed reparameterization changes conditioning or implicit regularization without removing harmful overlap; overlap alone does not prove redundancy hurts.

Norm matching can amplify very small deviations and create a threshold effect; record nonempty degeneracy and residual/reference norm ratios. A gain may arise from changed direction/gradient scaling rather than better relevance.
The normalization reference is a global pooled norm and is not invariant to group value offsets; only the unnormalized centered value is offset invariant at fixed scores.
Target-independent queries still use target-dependent match groups. Seed42 reuse and extensive adaptive validation search invite selection bias; deterministic repeats are not mechanism repetitions.
AUC and logloss can disagree; first512 diagnostics are candidate-supplied and unrepresentative of the full population. Source task pCVR/domains and this CTR/category-brand task differ.
